statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail is at the top of the watch band during the active post-FOMC price-discovery window.
recommendation: Current public policy mapping is WATCH; the post-FOMC sequence remains the main near-term risk window while a persistent no-retracement path has not been independently established.
headline: Post-FOMC repricing remains a WATCH regime
body: The Federal Reserve raised the target range by 25 basis points to 3.75%-4.00%. Reuters described Wall Street as whipsawing, with the Nasdaq about 0.7% higher, while later market coverage showed a fresh post-announcement Nasdaq high and yields edging higher. Warsh emphasized persistent inflation. Fresh supplementary breadth was positive, but no verified NQ failed-retracement sequence supports Tail above WATCH.

lookbackSummary: All 24 prior UTC clock-hour slots are available. Tail stayed between 17% and 24%; Stress was 99%-100%. The regime was mostly mixed, shifting to event/whipsaw around the U.S. data/FOMC sequence, with Tail reaching 24% WATCH in the 18:00 UTC hour.
outlookSummary: Near-term risk remains concentrated in the post-FOMC cash-close and rates-digestion window. Tail should fall quickly if the move becomes two-way with functional retracements. The next notable scheduled cluster is 12:30 UTC Thursday, when housing, labor and Philadelphia Fed data arrive together; that raises Stress before it raises Tail.

forecast.analysis: Post-hike trading is two-way but tech-led: Reuters had Nasdaq up about 0.7%, while MarketWatch showed a fresh post-announcement Nasdaq high and Treasury yields edging higher. Warsh stressed persistent inflation. Tail stays WATCH because a verified failed-retracement sequence is still absent.
drivers: Fed raised the target range 25 bp to 3.75%-4.00%
Nasdaq reached a fresh post-announcement high after initial gyration
Treasury yields edged higher during post-decision trading
Warsh said underlying inflation trends have not meaningfully improved

forecast.analysis: The cash close and remaining post-press-conference repricing can still produce a second leg. Tail stays at the top of WATCH unless a durable one-way extension with shallow or failed retracements is actually observed; two-way trade would argue for rapid de-escalation.
drivers: Need observed shallow or failed retracements before Tail escalation

news.title: Warsh says Fed focus to stay on inflation, underlying trends have not meaningfully improved

forecast.analysis: After the cash close, policy-path interpretation can continue through rates and index futures. Tail remains WATCH conditionally, but should ease if the first post-FOMC impulse is retraced and cross-asset moves stop reinforcing a single direction.
drivers: Retracement quality after the initial FOMC impulse
Rates/futures alignment as a conditional check

forecast.analysis: With the primary FOMC information wave past, risk shifts from event shock to digestion. The score assumes no verified persistent extension; renewed yield/equity alignment without meaningful retracement would invalidate that assumption.
drivers: Primary FOMC information wave largely complete

forecast.analysis: Late-evening liquidity can exaggerate moves, but the forecast allows Tail to decline if price discovery remains two-way. The main residual driver is whether the hawkish inflation message creates a delayed rates-led equity leg.
drivers: Lower liquidity can amplify residual moves
Oil remains a cross-asset inflation input

forecast.analysis: By midnight UTC, the base case is normalization after the FOMC sequence. Tail returns below WATCH if retracements remain functional; Stress stays extreme because the policy, oil and inflation backdrop remains difficult even without a pathological path.
drivers: Functional retracements are the key de-escalation condition
Stress remains high despite lower Tail

forecast.analysis: Overnight risk is mainly headline and gap risk rather than an assumed directional trend. Tail stays low unless futures begin holding near an extreme with repeated extensions and weak counter-moves.
drivers: No scheduled Tier-1 U.S. release in this hour

forecast.analysis: During the quieter Asian session, the forecast assumes no new U.S. catalyst. Persistent post-FOMC rate repricing could keep Stress high, while Tail remains low unless the price path itself becomes one-way.
drivers: Tail depends on observed directional persistence

forecast.analysis: Absent fresh catalysts, this hour is expected to be comparatively normal. The score allows for residual FOMC digestion but does not pre-price a directional move; a new geopolitical or rates discontinuity would be the main invalidation.
drivers: Geopolitical discontinuity remains a conditional risk

forecast.analysis: The overnight base case remains normalization with lower event intensity. Tail stays low if futures continue to show usable retracements; an abrupt oil, rates or geopolitical shock would raise Stress first and Tail only with directional persistence.
drivers: Oil and rates remain cross-asset checks

forecast.analysis: Approaching Europe, liquidity and cross-asset price discovery increase. Tail remains low conditionally; the key check is whether Europe reinforces the post-FOMC U.S. direction or instead produces two-way correction.

European trading provides the first fuller cross-session test of the Fed reaction. The forecast keeps Tail low unless yields, semiconductors and NQ align with persistent extension and shallow pullbacks.
drivers: Yield and semiconductor alignment as confirmation only
Need persistent NQ structure for higher Tail

forecast.analysis: European morning flow may clarify whether the FOMC move is being absorbed or extended. Tail remains low in the base case, with a higher score reserved for confirmed cross-asset directional efficiency.
drivers: Retracement quality remains the Tail criterion

forecast.analysis: As Europe matures, attention shifts toward the next U.S. data cluster. Stress rises modestly because stronger data could reinforce the tightening narrative, but Tail stays low before any release prints.

Pre-U.S. positioning can become more sensitive to the prior day's hawkish message. Tail remains below WATCH while future alignment is unobserved; widening yield pressure or one-way index futures would be the key conditional trigger.
drivers: No future data outcome is assumed

forecast.analysis: U.S. premarket liquidity begins to deepen. Tail moves into WATCH only as event proximity rises; the score does not assume a directional outcome and requires observed continuation to justify escalation.
drivers: Observed continuation required for Tail escalation

forecast.analysis: The hour before the 12:30 UTC data cluster carries higher event/whipsaw risk. Tail is WATCH because uncertainty rises, but the releases themselves do not prove mean-reversion failure before they print.
drivers: Housing, labor and regional manufacturing data at 12:30 UTC
Stress rises before Tail because outcomes are unobserved

forecast.analysis: Housing starts, jobless claims and the Philadelphia Fed survey are scheduled for 12:30 UTC. Stress rises sharply into the releases; Tail reaches the top of WATCH conditionally and would exceed it only if the observed post-release path becomes persistently one-way.
drivers: Post-release price-path quality is the key Tail checkpoint
Rates and tech breadth may confirm or conflict after the releases

forecast.analysis: The first U.S. cash-open hour follows the 12:30 data cluster. Tail remains at the top of WATCH because opening-auction continuation can matter, but the score assumes no future trend and requires observed shallow pullbacks or repeated extension for escalation.
drivers: U.S. cash open after the data cluster
Opening-auction continuation is a conditional Tail amplifier
Shallow pullbacks or repeated extension would be required for escalation

forecast.analysis: Pending Home Sales at 14:00 UTC adds a smaller checkpoint while the cash session digests morning data. Tail stays WATCH conditionally, with rapid de-escalation appropriate if opening moves retrace and cross-assets stabilize.

By mid-session, the data/opening impulse should be clearer. Tail eases within WATCH if the market has remained two-way; persistent extreme-holding with aligned yields and tech breadth would keep risk higher.
drivers: Session-extreme holding remains a conditional check

forecast.analysis: Event intensity declines into the U.S. afternoon. Tail sits at the lower edge of WATCH, assuming no verified continuation sequence; Stress remains high because rates and inflation sensitivity persist.
drivers: No assumed continuation without current evidence

forecast.analysis: Late-session risk returns below WATCH in the base case. A renewed directional push would need current evidence—failed retracements, extreme holding or cross-asset alignment—to justify a higher Tail score.
drivers: Failed retracements would be needed to lift Tail
Stress can remain high with low Tail

forecast.analysis: Into the next U.S. close, Tail remains low if the prior data and FOMC impulses have been absorbed with functional retracements. Stress is still elevated, but generic volatility alone does not imply a pathological path.
drivers: Functional mean reversion is the low-Tail base case
Residual policy and geopolitical headline risk

forecastDetail.comment: Current WATCH reflects the active post-FOMC repricing window: tech is positive and yields are edging higher, but no verified failed-retracement sequence supports an elevated Tail band.
The cash close remains a conditional second-leg window. Tail stays 24 unless actual one-way extension develops; two-way price discovery would support de-escalation.
After-hours risk remains event/whipsaw while markets digest the policy path. Tail eases if the initial move retraces and cross-assets stop reinforcing one direction.
With the main FOMC information wave past, the forecast shifts toward digestion; residual yield sensitivity matters more than event shock unless a delayed leg appears.
Late-evening liquidity can exaggerate residual moves, but Tail declines if mean reversion remains functional and no new directional amplifier emerges.
By 00:00 UTC, the base case is post-event normalization: Tail drops below WATCH while Stress remains extreme because the broader inflation/rates backdrop is still difficult.
